component.name: xmpp
component.title: XMPP
component.description: Send and receive XMPP (Jabber) messages, in private chats and in multi-user chat rooms.
component.label: chat,messaging

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

CamelXmppDoc.label: consumer
CamelXmppDoc.description: The received Smack message, set by the consumer when the doc option is true. The pubsub producer sets it to the PubSub packet that it sends.

consumerOut.description: The text of the chat message; the Smack Message when it has no body text, such as a pubsub notification. With doc, the Smack Message. The subject, thread and sender are in the CamelXmpp* headers

producerIn.description: The body is converted to text and sent as the chat message (a Map or a POJO as its toString); the headers become message properties. Without a room, doc sends a Smack Stanza (or an array of them) and pubsub a Smack PubSub packet as they are; another body fails

host.description: The host name or IP address of the XMPP server. It is also the XMPP domain when the serviceName option is not set. Not used when the connectionConfig option is set.

port.description: The TCP port of the XMPP server for client connections. Not used when the connectionConfig option is set.

participant.label: common
participant.description: The JID (Jabber ID) of the person to chat with: the producer sends the chat messages to it, and the consumer routes only the chat messages from it (or of every sender, without a participant). The consumer adds the XMPP domain of the server to a name without a domain, while the producer needs the full JID. The room option takes precedence over this option.

login.label: common
login.description: Whether to log in as the user after connecting. Used only when the user option is set; without a user, the connection always logs in anonymously. If false, the connection is not logged in, so it can neither send nor receive messages.

nickname.label: common
nickname.description: The nickname to enter the room with. Used only with the room option. If not set, the user option is used.

pubsub.label: common
pubsub.description: Whether to work with XEP-0060 Publish-Subscribe. The consumer also routes the messages of type headline and normal, such as pubsub event notifications, and the producer, without a room, sends the body as a Smack PubSub packet. Setting it to true also sets the doc option to true.

room.label: common
room.description: The XEP-0045 Multi-User Chat room to enter, as a room JID with the domain of the chat service, for example conference.jabber.org. A name without a domain is completed with the first Multi-User Chat service that the server announces. The producer sends the messages to the room, and the consumer routes the messages of the room and the chat messages of every sender.

serviceName.label: common
serviceName.description: The XMPP domain of the server (its service name), for example example.org when the host is xmpp.example.org. If not set, the host option is used. Not used when the connectionConfig option is set.

testConnectionOnStartup.label: common
testConnectionOnStartup.description: Whether the consumer and the chat and room producers connect to the XMPP server when they start, so that a server that cannot be reached fails the start. If false, such a producer connects at the first message, and the consumer tries again every connectionPollDelay seconds until it is started. The doc and pubsub producers always connect at the first message.

createAccount.label: common,advanced
createAccount.description: Whether to register the user as a new account on the server (XEP-0077 In-Band Registration), with the user and password options, before logging in. The registration is done for each new connection, and the connection fails when the server refuses it, for example because the account exists already.

resource.label: common,advanced
resource.description: The resource part of the full JID (the part after the slash) that the connection logs in with. Used only when the user option is set.

connectionPollDelay.label: consumer
connectionPollDelay.description: The delay in seconds between the checks of the consumer's connection, which connect and log in again a lost connection and enter the room again. It is also the delay between the attempts of a consumer that could not connect at startup (testConnectionOnStartup=false).

doc.label: consumer
doc.description: Whether the consumer puts the received Smack Message (org.jivesoftware.smack.packet.Message) in the body and in the CamelXmppDoc header, instead of the text of the message. The producer, without a room or pubsub, sends the body as it is: a Smack Stanza or an array of them.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

connectionConfig.label: advanced
connectionConfig.description: To use a custom Smack connection configuration, which must be an org.jivesoftware.smack.tcp.XMPPTCPConnectionConfiguration (XMPP over TCP), for example to change the TLS or SASL settings. When set, the host, port and serviceName options are not used to connect. Endpoints share a connection only when they refer to the same instance.

headerFilterStrategy.label: filter
headerFilterStrategy.description: To use a custom HeaderFilterStrategy to filter the headers. The producer adds the headers that pass as Jive properties to the XMPP message (the subject and language headers set the subject and language of the message), and the consumer turns the Jive properties of a received message into headers.

password.label: security
password.description: The password of the user. It can also be set in the user info of the URI, as user:password. With createAccount, it is also the password of the new account.

roomPassword.label: security
roomPassword.description: The password to enter a password-protected room.

user.label: security
user.description: The user name to log in with: the localpart of the JID, without the domain. It can also be set in the user info of the URI. If not set, the connection logs in anonymously (SASL ANONYMOUS), which needs a connectionConfig that enables it with performSaslAnonymousAuthentication().
